objects.description: Doubly-linked list node used as the list head or as an embedded link within containing structs. Each node maintains prev/next pointers forming a circular list when used with a head initialized to point to itself. Ownership and lifetime are managed by the embedding/containing object; this node contains no payload by itself.
Represents a source file location used by the Kconfig system, with linkage to parent and next files in a list plus file name and line number.
Three-valued logic used throughout Kconfig to represent no, module, or yes.
Enumerates expression node kinds for Kconfig boolean/expression trees.
Holds either a pointer to an expr node or to a symbol; used for expr tree children.
Binary/unary expression node for Kconfig dependency logic; children stored in left/right as either subexpressions or symbols depending on type.
Pairs an expression with its computed tristate value; used for visibility and dependencies.
Holds a raw value pointer and its tristate for a symbol’s user/auto/defaulted values.
Kinds of configuration symbols supported by Kconfig.
Represents a configuration symbol, including name, type, current and default values, visibility, flags, properties, and dependency relations.

objects.definition:
enum prop_type {
	P_UNKNOWN,
	P_PROMPT,	/* prompt "foo prompt" or "BAZ Value" */
	P_COMMENT,	/* text associated with a comment */
	P_MENU,	    /* prompt associated with a menu or menuconfig symbol */
	P_DEFAULT,	/* default y */
	P_CHOICE,	/* choice value */
	P_SELECT,	/* select BAR */
	P_IMPLY,	/* imply BAR */
	P_RANGE,	/* range 7..100 (for a symbol) */
	P_SYMBOL,	/* where a symbol is defined */
	P_RESET,	/* reset to defaults condition */
};
objects.description: Enumerates property kinds attached to symbols and menu nodes.
Property node attached to symbols/menus that stores prompts, defaults, selects, ranges, and their conditions and location.
A node in the menu tree representing symbols, menus, comments, and choices, including prompts, dependencies, help text, and source location.
Key mapping entry used by front ends to jump to a specific menu node; links into a list, records display offset and target menu.
Forward-declared growable string helper used for pretty-printing expressions. Only an incomplete type is provided here; full definition is elsewhere.

Array of C strings holding XPM image data for a specific UI icon (e.g., load, save, back, etc.). These are external definitions declared here, not defined; each points to an array of const char* lines comprising an XPM image.
Growable string buffer used by Kconfig utilities. Tracks current length, backing char buffer, and optional wrapping width for formatting long lines.
Menu node type used by Kconfig to represent menu entries and hierarchy. Only forward-declared here; full definition resides elsewhere (likely in menu.h or menu.c). Details unknown in this header.
Kconfig symbol object representing configuration options and values. Forward-declared via included expr.h; no complete definition in this header. Details unknown here.
Kconfig property object associated with symbols or menus (e.g., prompts, dependencies, ranges). Forward-declared; full definition is elsewhere.
Represents a source file tracked by Kconfig parser. Only forward-declared; definition is not present in this header.

Enumeration-like type for three-valued logic (n/m/y) used by Kconfig. The underlying enum/type is declared in expr.h; not defined here. Included due to inline accessors using tristate; details unknown in this header.
Intrusive list node type from Linux kernel list API, referenced by function prototypes. Not defined in this header.

functions.name: list_empty
functions.signature: static inline int list_empty(const struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the given list head is empty. Intended for Linux-kernel–style intrusive doubly-linked circular lists where the head's next and prev point to itself when empty. Typical usage: initialize a list head, then call this to check whether any elements have been added.
requirements: head must be a non-NULL pointer.

head must reference a properly initialized list head (e.g., via LIST_HEAD_INIT or LIST_HEAD) belonging to a circular doubly-linked list where an empty list has head->next == head and head->prev == head.
If the list structure is corrupted or uninitialized, behavior is undefined.

functions.name: list_add_tail
functions.signature: static inline void list_add_tail(struct list_head *_new, struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Insert a new list node at the tail (just before the head) of the intrusive doubly-linked circular list anchored by head. Useful for implementing FIFO queues.
requirements: _new must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct list_head embedded in the element to be added.
head must be a non-NULL pointer to a valid, initialized list head of a circular doubly-linked list (e.g., via LIST_HEAD_INIT or LIST_HEAD).
_new will have its next and prev fields overwritten; it should not already be linked into any list (inferred from standard list semantics and the function’s behavior).
Do not pass corrupted or uninitialized list nodes; prev/next of head must be consistent.

functions.name: list_del
functions.description: Remove an existing node from its intrusive doubly-linked circular list. After removal, the node’s next and prev are set to poison values to catch misuse. Note: list_empty() on the removed entry does not return true; the entry is in an undefined state until reinitialized or re-added.
requirements: entry must be a non-NULL pointer to a struct list_head that is currently linked into a list (its prev and next must be valid).
Caller must not use entry->next or entry->prev after deletion except to reinitialize the node; they are set to poison values.
Do not call list_del on the same entry more than once without re-adding/reinitializing it (inferred from the poisoning and typical list semantics).
List structure must be valid and not corrupted at the time of deletion.

functions.name: lookup_file
functions.description: Lookup or retrieve a struct file descriptor (Kconfig source location) by its name. Expected to search an internal list of loaded files and return the matching entry, possibly creating it if not present (implementation-specific).
requirements: name must be a valid, null-terminated C string representing a filename/path.
The returned pointer may be NULL if no matching file exists or on allocation failure (implementation-specific).
Callers must not assume ownership of the returned struct file unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: expr_alloc_symbol
functions.description: Allocate and return a new expression node that wraps a symbol (E_SYMBOL). Used to construct expression trees from symbols.
requirements: sym must be a valid, initialized struct symbol pointer.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
The returned expression is owned by the caller and must be freed with expr_free() when no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: expr_alloc_one
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_one(enum expr_type type, struct expr *ce);
functions.description: Allocate a unary expression node of the given type with a single child expression. Used for operators like NOT or for single-operand constructs.
requirements: type must be a valid enum expr_type that is unary in nature (e.g., E_NOT).
ce must be either NULL or a well-formed expression tree node expected by the operator.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
The returned expression must be released via expr_free() when done (inferred).

functions.name: expr_alloc_two
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_two(enum expr_type type, struct expr *e1, struct expr *e2);
functions.description: Allocate a binary expression node of the given type with two child expressions. Used for AND, OR, comparisons, ranges, lists, etc.
requirements: type must be a valid binary enum expr_type (e.g., E_AND, E_OR, E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, E_LTH, E_LEQ, E_GTH, E_GEQ, E_RANGE, E_LIST).
e1 and e2 must be either NULL or well-formed expression trees compatible with the operator.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
Caller owns the returned node and must free it with expr_free() (inferred).

functions.name: expr_alloc_comp
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_alloc_comp(enum expr_type type, struct symbol *s1, struct symbol *s2);
functions.description: Allocate a comparison expression node using two symbols and the specified comparison operator. Intended for operators like ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=.
requirements: type must be one of the comparison types: E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, E_LTH, E_LEQ, E_GTH, E_GEQ (inferred from name and enum).
s1 and s2 must be valid, initialized struct symbol pointers.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
Caller must free the returned expression with expr_free() when finished (inferred).

functions.name: expr_alloc_and
functions.description: Convenience allocator that creates an E_AND node combining two expressions.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be either NULL or well-formed expression trees.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
Caller must free the returned node with expr_free() (inferred).

functions.name: expr_alloc_or
functions.description: Convenience allocator that creates an E_OR node combining two expressions.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be either NULL or well-formed expression trees.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
Caller must free the returned node with expr_free() (inferred).

functions.name: expr_copy
functions.description: Create and return a deep copy of the given expression tree.
requirements: org must be a valid, well-formed expression tree pointer; behavior for NULL is unknown.
May return NULL on allocation failure; callers must check the return value.
The returned copy is owned by the caller and must be freed with expr_free() (inferred).

functions.name: expr_free
functions.description: Free an expression tree previously allocated by expr_alloc_* or expr_copy. Recursively releases any child nodes as appropriate.
requirements: e must be either NULL or a pointer to an expression node obtained from expr_alloc_* or expr_copy (assumption based on naming patterns).
Must not be called on memory not allocated by the expression allocation routines (to avoid undefined behavior).
After return, e and any of its children must not be accessed.

functions.name: expr_eliminate_eq
functions.description: Simplify two expressions by eliminating common equal subexpressions or normalizing equality-related parts. Intended to mutate the provided expression pointers in place to aid further simplification or comparison.
requirements: ep1 and ep2 must be non-NULL pointers to variables of type struct expr*.
*ep1 and *ep2 must be either NULL or well-formed expression trees.
The function may modify the expressions pointed to by ep1 and ep2; callers must own and manage the lifetime of those trees.
Do not pass pointers to const data because the function mutates via the double pointer (inferred).

functions.name: expr_eq
functions.description: Compare two expression trees for structural/logical equality. Returns nonzero if equal, zero otherwise.
requirements: e1 and e2 must be either NULL or valid expression tree pointers.
No side effects are expected; the inputs are not modified (inferred).

functions.name: expr_calc_value
functions.description: Evaluate the given expression to a tristate value (no/mod/yes) according to Kconfig semantics.
requirements: e should be a well-formed expression tree. In Kconfig a NULL expression often represents logical 'yes' (as evidenced by expr_is_yes), but exact NULL handling here is not explicitly documented.
Callers must handle all three possible tristate return values.

functions.name: expr_trans_bool
functions.description: Transform or coerce the expression into a purely boolean/tristate form suitable for visibility/condition checks. Likely simplifies comparisons and ranges to boolean tests.
requirements: e must be either NULL or a well-formed expression tree.
May return NULL on allocation failure or if the transformation eliminates the expression entirely (implementation-specific); callers must check the return.
Caller owns the returned expression and must free it with expr_free() (inferred).

functions.name: expr_eliminate_dups
functions.description: Simplify an expression by removing duplicate subexpressions, producing a logically equivalent but more compact tree.
requirements: e must be either NULL or a well-formed expression tree.
May return a new expression tree (or possibly reuse input); callers should use the returned pointer thereafter.
May return NULL if the expression simplifies to nothing or on allocation failure; caller must check the return value.
Caller is responsible for freeing the returned expression when done (inferred).

functions.name: expr_transform
functions.description: Apply general transformation/simplification passes to an expression tree (e.g., normalization, De Morgan, constant folding).
requirements: e must be either NULL or a well-formed expression tree.
May return a new or modified tree; callers should use and manage the returned pointer.
May return NULL on allocation failure or full elimination; caller must check the return value.
Caller must free the resulting tree when no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: expr_contains_symbol
functions.description: Test whether the given symbol occurs within the dependency expression tree. Returns nonzero if present, zero otherwise.
requirements: dep must be either NULL or a valid expression tree.
sym must be a valid, non-NULL struct symbol pointer.

functions.name: expr_depends_symbol
functions.description: Determine whether the dependency expression depends on the given symbol (i.e., changing the symbol could affect the expression). Returns true if there is a dependency.
requirements: dep must be either NULL or a valid expression tree.
sym must be a valid, non-NULL struct symbol pointer.

functions.name: expr_trans_compare
functions.signature: struct expr *expr_trans_compare(struct expr *e, enum expr_type type, struct symbol *sym);
functions.description: Transform an expression by applying a comparison against the given symbol using the specified comparison operator, possibly normalizing or simplifying the result.
requirements: e must be either NULL or a valid expression tree.
type must be a comparison-oriented enum expr_type (e.g., E_EQUAL, E_UNEQUAL, E_LTH, E_LEQ, E_GTH, E_GEQ) appropriate for compare transformations (inferred from name).
sym must be a valid, non-NULL struct symbol pointer.
May return NULL on allocation failure or if the transformation removes the expression; callers must check the return value.
Caller owns the returned expression and must free it with expr_free() (inferred).

functions.name: expr_fprint
functions.description: Print a textual representation of the expression to the given FILE stream, suitable for debugging or logging.
requirements: out must be a valid, writable FILE* stream.
e should be either NULL or a valid expression tree; exact handling of NULL is not documented.
The function does not return a value; callers should ensure out is flushed/closed as needed by their I/O logic.

functions.name: expr_gstr_print
functions.description: Append a textual representation of the expression to a dynamic string builder (gstr). Useful for building diagnostic messages or UI text.
requirements: gs must be a valid, initialized struct gstr pointer capable of receiving appended text.
e should be either NULL or a valid expression tree; exact handling of NULL is not documented.

functions.name: expr_gstr_print_revdep
functions.signature: void expr_gstr_print_revdep(struct expr *e, struct gstr *gs, tristate pr_type, const char *title);
functions.description: Append a formatted description of reverse dependencies implied by the expression to the gstr, using the provided title and print type filter.
requirements: gs must be a valid, initialized struct gstr pointer.
e should be a valid expression tree (NULL handling not documented).
pr_type must be a valid tristate value (no/mod/yes).
title must be a valid, null-terminated C string; pass a non-NULL pointer.

functions.name: expr_is_yes
functions.description: Return nonzero if the expression represents logical 'yes'. In Kconfig semantics, a NULL expression or an E_SYMBOL node equal to the global symbol_yes is considered 'yes'.
requirements: e may be NULL; NULL is treated as logical 'yes'.
If non-NULL, e must be a valid expression; correct behavior relies on e->type being E_SYMBOL and e->left.sym comparing to &symbol_yes for a 'yes' result.

functions.name: expr_is_no
functions.description: Return nonzero if the expression represents logical 'no'. This is true for an E_SYMBOL node whose symbol is the global symbol_no. NULL is treated as not 'no'.
requirements: e may be NULL; NULL is treated as not 'no' (returns 0).
If non-NULL, e must be a valid expression; correct behavior requires e->type == E_SYMBOL and e->left.sym == &symbol_no for a 'no' result.

functions.name: CONFIG_prefix
functions.description: Returns the prefix used for configuration keys. It checks the environment variable "CONFIG_" and returns its value if set; otherwise it returns a built-in default prefix (CONFIG_). Intended for code that needs to construct or parse Kconfig-style variable names.
requirements: No arguments.
Caller should not modify the returned string literal/default; when the environment variable is used, the returned pointer is owned by the C library and must not be freed.

functions.name: zconfdump
functions.description: Dumps configuration/parser state to the given file stream. Typically used for debugging or emitting the parsed configuration data.
requirements: out must be a valid, open FILE* for writing.
The stream should remain valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: zconf_starthelp
functions.description: Signals the start of a help text section in the configuration parser. Used internally during parsing of Kconfig help blocks.
requirements: No arguments.
Must be called in the correct parsing phase; specific sequencing requirements are unknown.

functions.name: zconf_fopen
functions.description: Opens a configuration-related file by name and returns a FILE* for reading. Wrapper around fopen or search-path aware open for the Kconfig system.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated path string.
Caller is responsible for closing the returned FILE* when done (ownership semantics beyond standard FILE* are unknown).
On failure, may return NULL; callers should check the return value.

functions.name: zconf_initscan
functions.description: Initializes the configuration lexer/scanner for the given file. Prepares internal state for subsequent scanning tokens.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated path to a file to scan.
Must be called before other scanning/lexing functions that require an initialized scanner.

functions.name: zconf_nextfile
functions.description: Pushes or switches the scanner to process the next input file. Used when handling source/include directives in Kconfig files.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated path string to the next file.
Must be called after zconf_initscan has established an initial scanning context.

functions.name: zconf_lineno
functions.description: Returns the current line number in the file being scanned by the configuration lexer.
requirements: No arguments.
Must be called while a scan is active; otherwise the returned value is unspecified.

functions.name: zconf_curname
functions.description: Returns the name (path) of the current file being scanned by the configuration lexer.
requirements: No arguments.
The returned pointer must not be freed by the caller.
Must be called while a scan is active; otherwise the returned pointer may be NULL or unspecified.

functions.name: conf_get_configname
functions.description: Returns the path/name of the main configuration file in use (e.g., .config).
requirements: No arguments.
The returned pointer is owned by the configuration system and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: set_all_choice_values
functions.description: Sets values for all symbols in a choice, based on the provided choice symbol. Typically enforces that only one value is selected in a choice block.
requirements: csym must be a valid, initialized choice-type struct symbol pointer (non-null).

functions.name: file_lookup
functions.description: Looks up or creates an internal file-tracking structure for the given file name in the Kconfig system.
requirements: name must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string representing a file name/path.
Returned struct file* ownership and lifetime are managed by the Kconfig system; caller should not free it (exact lifetime is unknown).

functions.name: xmalloc
functions.description: Allocates a memory block of the given size. Wrapper around malloc that is commonly expected to never return NULL (behavior on OOM is unknown without implementation).
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; zero-size behavior follows implementation policy and is unknown.
Caller owns the returned memory and must free it with free or the corresponding deallocator used in this project.

functions.name: xcalloc
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array. Wrapper around calloc; behavior on allocation failure is unknown without implementation.
requirements: nmemb and size specify the number of elements and their size; their product must fit in size_t without overflow.
Caller owns the returned memory and must free it with free or the corresponding deallocator used in this project.

functions.name: xrealloc
functions.description: Resizes a previously allocated memory block. Wrapper around realloc; behavior on allocation failure is unknown without implementation.
requirements: If p is non-null, it must be a pointer previously returned by an allocation function compatible with realloc.
size is the new size in bytes; zero-size behavior is implementation-defined/unknown here.
Caller is responsible for managing the returned pointer and freeing it appropriately.

functions.name: xstrdup
functions.description: Duplicates a NUL-terminated string. Wrapper around strdup; behavior on allocation failure is unknown without implementation.
requirements: s must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string.
Caller owns the returned string and must free it with free or the corresponding deallocator used in this project.

functions.name: xstrndup
functions.description: Duplicates at most n bytes of the input string, NUL-terminating the result. Wrapper around strndup; behavior on allocation failure is unknown without implementation.
requirements: s must be a non-null pointer to a string; it may be longer than n.
Caller owns the returned string and must free it with free or the corresponding deallocator used in this project.

functions.name: yylex
functions.description: Lexical analyzer function generated by lex/flex for the Kconfig language. Returns the next token code from the input stream.
requirements: No arguments.
Must be called after the scanner has been initialized (e.g., via zconf_initscan).
Caller should handle return value per the lexer’s token definitions; 0 typically indicates EOF.

functions.name: str_new
functions.description: Creates and returns a new growable string object (gstr) with zero length. Used to build formatted/help strings within the Kconfig system.
requirements: No arguments.
Returned struct gstr must be managed with str_free when no longer needed, and passed to other gstr functions while in a valid state.

functions.name: str_free
functions.description: Releases resources held by a gstr object and invalidates it.
requirements: gs must be a non-null pointer to a gstr previously obtained from str_new or otherwise properly initialized.
gs must remain valid for the duration of the call; it must not be used after being freed.

functions.name: str_append
functions.description: Appends the given C string to the growable string gs. May reallocate internal buffers.
requirements: gs must be a valid, initialized gstr pointer.
s must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: str_printf
functions.description: Formats text according to printf-style fmt and appends it to the growable string gs.
requirements: gs must be a valid, initialized gstr pointer.
fmt must be a non-null format string compatible with printf semantics.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.

functions.name: str_get
functions.description: Retrieves the internal C string buffer from the growable string gs. Often used to obtain the accumulated text.
requirements: gs must be a valid, initialized gstr pointer.
Ownership/lifetime of the returned pointer is unknown from this header; callers must consult implementation to know whether to free it or treat it as borrowed.

functions.name: _menu_init
functions.description: Initializes internal menu structures for the Kconfig menu system. Sets up state before parsing or building the menu tree.
requirements: No arguments.
Must be called before other menu-building functions are used.

functions.name: menu_warn
functions.description: Emits a warning associated with the specified menu node, with printf-style formatting.
requirements: menu should be a valid pointer to a menu node; may be NULL if a global warning is allowed (unknown).
fmt must be a non-null format string compatible with printf semantics.
Variadic arguments must match the format specifiers in fmt.

functions.name: menu_add_menu
functions.description: Creates and adds a new submenu/context to the current menu structure and returns it.
requirements: No arguments.
Must be called after menu system initialization.
Caller should not free the returned menu pointer; lifetime is managed by the menu system (exact ownership details unknown).

functions.name: menu_end_menu
functions.description: Closes the current submenu/context in the menu structure.
requirements: No arguments.
Must correspond to a preceding menu_add_menu or similar start; nesting must be balanced.

functions.name: menu_add_entry
functions.description: Adds a configuration entry associated with the given symbol to the current menu.
requirements: sym must be a valid, initialized struct symbol pointer.

functions.name: menu_add_dep
functions.description: Adds a dependency expression to the current menu entry or context.
requirements: dep must be a valid pointer to an expression object representing dependencies.

functions.name: menu_add_visibility
functions.description: Adds a visibility expression controlling whether a menu entry is shown.
requirements: dep must be a valid pointer to an expression object.

functions.name: menu_add_prop
functions.signature: struct property *menu_add_prop(enum prop_type type, struct expr *expr, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds a property of the given type to the current menu context, with an associated expression/value and optional dependency.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type value.
expr may be NULL or a valid expression pointer depending on the property type (exact rules unknown).
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.
Returned property is owned by the menu system; caller must not free it (exact ownership details unknown).

functions.name: menu_add_prompt
functions.signature: struct property *menu_add_prompt(enum prop_type type, char *prompt, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds a prompt string (and optional dependency) as a property of the given type to the current menu entry.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type value supporting prompts.
prompt must be a non-null, NUL-terminated string; ownership transfer/duplication behavior is unknown.
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.
Returned property is managed by the menu system; caller must not free it (exact ownership details unknown).

functions.name: menu_add_expr
functions.signature: void menu_add_expr(enum prop_type type, struct expr *expr, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds an expression-valued property of the given type to the current menu entry, with an optional dependency expression.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type.
expr must be a valid expression pointer required by the property type (NULL acceptance is unknown).
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.

functions.name: menu_add_symbol
functions.signature: void menu_add_symbol(enum prop_type type, struct symbol *sym, struct expr *dep)
functions.description: Adds a symbol-valued property of the given type to the current menu entry, with an optional dependency expression.
requirements: type must be a valid enum prop_type.
sym must be a valid, initialized symbol pointer.
dep may be NULL or a valid dependency expression.

functions.name: menu_finalize
functions.description: Finalizes the menu tree under the given parent, computing derived data (visibility, prompts, etc.).
requirements: parent must be a valid pointer to a menu node that represents the root of the subtree to finalize.

functions.name: menu_set_type
functions.description: Sets the type of the current menu entry (e.g., tristate, string).
requirements: type must be a valid value understood by the menu system; mapping from int to type is unknown.

functions.name: menu_is_empty
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node has no visible/active entries.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_is_visible
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node is currently visible under active conditions/dependencies.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_has_prompt
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node has a prompt associated with it.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_get_prompt
functions.description: Returns the prompt string for the given menu node.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller; lifetime is managed by the menu system (exact details unknown).

functions.name: menu_get_parent_menu
functions.description: Returns the parent menu node for the given menu node.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
Returned pointer is managed by the menu system; caller must not free it.

functions.name: menu_has_help
functions.description: Returns true if the given menu node has associated help text.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.

functions.name: menu_get_help
functions.description: Returns the help text for the given menu node, if any.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller; lifetime is managed by the menu system (exact details unknown).

functions.name: get_jump_key_char
functions.description: Returns the configured jump key character used by UI/navigation in the menu system.
requirements: No arguments.

functions.name: get_relations_str
functions.signature: struct gstr get_relations_str(struct symbol **sym_arr, struct list_head *head)
functions.description: Builds and returns a textual description of relations/dependencies among symbols in sym_arr, optionally filtered or linked via the provided list.
requirements: sym_arr must be a valid, NULL-terminated array of symbol pointers or otherwise valid per implementation (exact expectations unknown).
head must be a valid pointer to a list_head used by the implementation; its required state/content is unknown.
Returned gstr should be freed with str_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: menu_get_ext_help
functions.description: Appends the extended help for the given menu node to the provided gstr buffer.
requirements: menu must be a valid pointer to a menu node.
help must be a valid, initialized gstr pointer created by str_new.

functions.name: sym_clear_all_valid
functions.description: Clears the valid/dirty flags of all symbols, forcing recomputation of values/dependencies.
requirements: No arguments.

functions.name: sym_choice_default
functions.description: Determines and returns the default symbol selected for a choice symbol.
requirements: sym must be a valid pointer to a choice-type symbol.
Returned symbol is managed by the symbol system; caller must not free it.

functions.name: sym_get_range_prop
functions.description: Returns the range property (min/max) associated with the given symbol, if any.
requirements: sym must be a valid symbol pointer.
Returned property is managed by the symbol system; caller must not free it.

functions.name: sym_get_string_default
functions.description: Returns the default string value for the given symbol, if any.
requirements: sym must be a valid symbol pointer.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller; ownership is with the symbol system.

functions.name: sym_check_deps
functions.description: Checks dependency consistency for the given symbol and returns a symbol related to any dependency issue or the input symbol per implementation.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: generic NUL-terminated C string consumed by many APIs
# This generator focuses on producing valid, interesting strings that exercise
# different code paths in the provided fuzz stubs, particularly those using
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR (e.g., titles, prompts, format args, filenames, help text).
#
# Goals:
# - Produce short and long strings
# - Include ASCII, whitespace, punctuation, and UTF-8 multibyte characters
# - Include lines, paragraphs, and content resembling Kconfig snippets
# - Include edge cases: empty, very long (<=4096), repeated chars
# - Always NUL-terminated for C-compat. The harness typically reads bytes and
#   exposes them as C strings; we ensure a trailing NUL.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PRINT = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
WHITESPACE = " \t\r\n\v\f"
# Some UTF-8 sequences (valid):
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    "✓", "©", "—", "…", "µ", "ß", "中", "文", "日本語", "русский", "ελληνικά",
    "😀", "🚀", "配置", "参数", "конфиг", "μενού", "メニュー"
]

KCONFIG_TEMPLATES: List[str] = [
    # Resemble Kconfig prompts/titles/help
    "CONFIG_FOO=y\n",
    "CONFIG_BAR=m\n",
    "# CONFIG_BAZ is not set\n",
    "menu \"Main Menu\"\n\thelp\n\t This is a help paragraph.\nendmenu\n",
    "config NET\n\tbool \"Networking support\"\n\tdefault y\n",
    "comment \"Experimental features\"\n",
    "choice\n\tprompt \"Choose driver\"\nendchoice\n",
    "menuconfig USB\n\tbool \"USB support\"\n",
]

FILENAMES = [
    ".config",
    "Kconfig",
    "arch/x86/Kconfig",
    "drivers/usb/Kconfig",
    "subsys/Kconfig.debug",
    "include/generated/autoconf.h",
]

TITLES = [
    "Reverse dependencies",
    "Revdeps",
    "Dependencies for %s",
    "Why is this option selected?",
    "Implied by",
]

PUNCT_HEAVY = "::::::;;;;;,,,,,-----_____" * 4


def _rand_utf8(rnd: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII and some multibyte snippets
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        t = rnd.random()
        if t < 0.7:
            out.append(rnd.choice(ASCII_PRINT))
        else:
            out.append(rnd.choice(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))
    return "".join(out)


def _weighted_choice(rnd: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rnd.randrange(len(items))] if items else ""


def _make_interesting_strings(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    res: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Empty string
    res.append(b"\x00")

    # 2) Small ASCII word
    res.append(("test" + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 3) Title-like strings
    res.append((_weighted_choice(rnd, TITLES) + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 4) Filename-like strings
    res.append((_weighted_choice(rnd, FILENAMES) + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 5) Kconfig snippet (single-line)
    res.append((_weighted_choice(rnd, ["CONFIG_FOO=y", "# CONFIG_BAR is not set"]) + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 6) Kconfig multi-line template
    res.append((_weighted_choice(rnd, KCONFIG_TEMPLATES) + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 7) Long ASCII paragraph with whitespace
    para = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 10)):
        words = ["opt", "value", "prompt", "menu", "help", "select", "imply"]
        line = " ".join(rnd.choice(words) for _ in range(rnd.randint(3, 12)))
        para.append(line)
    s = ("\n".join(para))
    res.append((s + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 8) UTF-8 rich string
    s8 = _rand_utf8(rnd, rnd.randint(8, 40))
    res.append((s8 + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 9) Punctuation-heavy
    res.append((PUNCT_HEAVY + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 10) Format-arg-like strings used by str_printf cases
    # Though format strings are fixed in the stub, arguments are FUZZ_PARAM_STR;
    # still provide content that may appear in %s positions.
    arglike = [
        "alpha", "12345", "deadbeef", "with spaces", "tab\tsep", "line1\nline2",
        "unicode-«»-✓", "percent%inside", "brace{brackets}",
    ]
    res.append((_weighted_choice(rnd, arglike) + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 11) Very long valid line to exercise wrapping in gstr (<= 4095 + NUL)
    long_len = rnd.randint(512, min(3500, MAX_TOTAL - 1))
    long_body = _rand_utf8(rnd, long_len)
    res.append((long_body + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 12) Prompt-like quoted string
    prompt = '"' + _rand_utf8(rnd, rnd.randint(5, 30)) + '"'
    res.append((prompt + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 13) Help paragraph with indentation
    help_lines = [
        "  help",
        "    This option enables something.",
        "    Use with care.",
    ]
    res.append((("\n".join(help_lines)) + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    # 14) Choice of common titles again but with placeholder expansion
    base = _weighted_choice(rnd, TITLES)
    if "%s" in base:
        base = base.replace("%s", _weighted_choice(rnd, ["NET", "USB", "SOUND"]))
    res.append((base + "\x00").encode("utf-8"))

    return res


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of candidate strings
    candidates = _make_interesting_strings(rnd)

    # Randomly select a subset and concatenate with NUL separators to let
    # the fuzzing runtime extract individual strings deterministically.
    # Ensure total size <= 4096.
    rnd.shuffle(candidates)

    out = bytearray()
    for b in candidates:
        # Each b already ends with NUL; we can concatenate multiple NUL-terminated
        # strings so that multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls can draw from the buffer.
        if len(out) + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(b)

    # Guarantee at least one NUL terminator
    if not out or out[-1] != 0:
        out.append(0)

    # Bound the size defensively
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
        if out[-1] != 0:
            # Ensure last byte is NUL
            out[-1] = 0

    return bytes(out)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for valid filesystem path bytes suitable for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME/STR
# Goals:
# - Produce NUL-terminated path strings
# - Often point to an existing readable/writable file to exercise fopen/zconf_fopen
# - Sometimes produce directories or non-existing files for negative paths
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes
# - Seeded randomness

_SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.,@+#%="

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Avoid leading/trailing spaces; include some edge chars occasionally
    name = ''.join(rng.choice(_SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Occasionally add an extension
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        ext_len = rng.randint(1, 4)
        ext = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(ext_len))
        name += '.' + ext
    return name

def _rand_components(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    comps = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(depth):
        # mix normal names with special entries
        p = rng.random()
        if p < 0.1:
            comps.append(".")
        elif p < 0.2:
            comps.append("..")
        else:
            comps.append(_rand_name(rng))
    # final component is a file-like name
    comps.append(_rand_name(rng, 1, 20))
    return comps

def _build_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose absolute or relative
    absolute = rng.random() < 0.4
    # Occasionally target temp directory to allow write access
    base_dirs = [os.getcwd(), os.getenv('TMPDIR') or '/tmp', '.', 'config', 'kconfig', 'subdir']
    base = ''
    if absolute:
        base = rng.choice([os.path.abspath(d) for d in base_dirs])
    else:
        base = rng.choice(['.', './', './subdir', ''])

    comps = _rand_components(rng)
    path = base
    for c in comps:
        if not path or path.endswith(os.sep) or path == '.':
            path = (path if path not in ('', '.') else '') + c
        else:
            path = path + os.sep + c
    # Occasionally add nested directories suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        path = os.path.join(path, _rand_name(rng))
    return path

def _ensure_parent_dirs(p: str):
    parent = os.path.dirname(p) or '.'
    try:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    except Exception:
        # Best-effort; ignore failures
        pass

def _maybe_create_file(rng: random.Random, path: str) -> None:
    # 70% create a file that exists; 20% create a directory; 10% leave missing
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.7:
        _ensure_parent_dirs(path)
        try:
            # Create and write some Kconfig-like content to be interesting
            mode = 'wb'
            with open(path, mode) as f:
                # Synthesized small Kconfig-ish content
                lines = []
                # Randomly generate a few config entries and comments
                n_entries = rng.randint(1, 5)
                for i in range(n_entries):
                    sym = 'CONFIG_' + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + "_") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
                    val_type = rng.choice(['bool', 'tristate', 'string', 'int', 'hex'])
                    lines.append(f"config {sym}\n")
                    lines.append(f"    {val_type}\n")
                    if rng.random() < 0.6:
                        lines.append(f"    prompt \"{_rand_name(rng,3,10)}\"\n")
                    if val_type in ('bool','tristate') and rng.random() < 0.5:
                        lines.append("    default y\n")
                    if val_type == 'string' and rng.random() < 0.5:
                        lines.append(f"    default \"{_rand_name(rng,3,8)}\"\n")
                    if rng.random() < 0.4:
                        lines.append("    help\n")
                        help_lines = rng.randint(1, 3)
                        for _ in range(help_lines):
                            lines.append(f"      {_rand_name(rng,5,15)} description\n")
                if rng.random() < 0.4:
                    lines.insert(0, f"# Generated seed content\n")
                data = ''.join(lines).encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
                f.write(data)
        except Exception:
            pass
    elif choice < 0.9:
        # Create a directory
        try:
            os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
        except Exception:
            pass
    else:
        # leave missing
        pass

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a few candidate paths and pick one after attempting creation
    candidates = []
    for _ in range(3):
        p = _build_path(rng)
        candidates.append(p)
    # Try to ensure at least one existing writable regular file
    chosen = rng.choice(candidates)
    _maybe_create_file(rng, chosen)

    # Occasionally return an existing special path like .config in CWD
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        special = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '.config')
        try:
            if not os.path.exists(special):
                with open(special, 'wb') as f:
                    f.write(b"# Auto-generated config\nCONFIG_FUZZ=y\n")
        except Exception:
            pass
        chosen = special

    # Ensure NUL-terminated bytes
    s = chosen
    # Truncate to keep under 4096 total
    if len(s) > 4000:
        s = s[:4000]
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00"

import os
import random
import struct
import zlib

# This generator creates interesting arbitrary binary file data that may be
# consumed by zconfdump() or any code paths it reaches. Since the stub just
# provides a writable FILE*, the callee may read global state, environment,
# or possibly other config files; but the fuzzable file contents themselves
# are opaque arbitrary bytes. We therefore generate diverse, valid binary
# content with patterns that often trigger different buffered I/O behaviors
# (small/large sizes, zeros, ASCII text, repeated patterns, compressed-like
# segments, and random data), while keeping size under 4096 bytes.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

ASCII_SNIPPETS = [
    b"# Kconfig autogenerated test\n",
    b"CONFIG_FOO=y\nCONFIG_BAR=m\n# CONFIG_BAZ is not set\n",
    b"menu \"Test Menu\"\n\thelp\n\t  Help text line\nendmenu\n",
    b"choice\n\tprompt \"Pick one\"\nendchoice\n",
    b"config TEST\n\tbool \"A test option\"\n\tdepends on BAR || BAZ\n",
    b"# Long line: " + b"X" * 200 + b"\n",
]


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _repeat_pattern(pattern: bytes, total: int) -> bytes:
    if not pattern:
        return b""
    reps, rem = divmod(total, len(pattern))
    return pattern * reps + pattern[:rem]


def _chunk_ascii(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Concatenate a few ASCII-like snippets optionally with random whitespace
    parts = []
    count = rng.randint(1, min(6, len(ASCII_SNIPPETS)))
    picks = rng.sample(ASCII_SNIPPETS, count)
    for p in picks:
        parts.append(p)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(b"\n" * rng.randint(0, 3))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _chunk_zeros(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    return b"\x00" * rng.randint(8, max(8, min(256, max_len)))


def _chunk_pattern(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Create a small pattern and repeat it
    pat_len = rng.randint(1, min(32, max_len))
    pat = _rand_bytes(rng, pat_len)
    total = rng.randint(pat_len, min(max_len, pat_len * rng.randint(2, 64)))
    return _repeat_pattern(pat, total)


def _chunk_random(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    return _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(16, max(16, min(1024, max_len))))


def _chunk_structured(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # A simple container: magic, length, payload, crc32
    payload_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, min(512, max_len - 16)))
    payload = _rand_bytes(rng, payload_len)
    magic = rng.choice([b"CONF", b"KCNF", b"DATA", b"\x89\x43\x46\x47"])  # 4 bytes
    header = magic + struct.pack(
        "<II", payload_len, rng.getrandbits(32)
    )
    crc = struct.pack("<I", zlib.crc32(payload) & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    blob = header + payload + crc
    if len(blob) > max_len:
        return blob[:max_len]
    return blob


def _compose(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Decide overall size target
    target = rng.randint(32, MAX_SIZE)
    chunks = []

    # Optionally start with a UTF-8 BOM or shebang-like prefix to vary paths
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        chunks.append(b"\xEF\xBB\xBF")
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        chunks.append(b"#!kconfig\n")

    # Mix chunk types
    producers = [
        lambda m: _chunk_ascii(rng),
        lambda m: _chunk_zeros(rng, m),
        lambda m: _chunk_pattern(rng, m),
        lambda m: _chunk_random(rng, m),
        lambda m: _chunk_structured(rng, m),
    ]

    remaining = target - sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
    while remaining > 0:
        prod = rng.choice(producers)
        piece = prod(remaining)
        if not piece:
            break
        chunks.append(piece)
        remaining = target - sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
        # Occasionally insert newlines to encourage text-like layout
        if remaining > 0 and rng.random() < 0.3:
            nl = b"\n" * rng.randint(1, min(5, remaining))
            chunks.append(nl)
            remaining -= len(nl)

    data = b"".join(chunks)
    # Ensure final size bound
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]

    # Optionally end with newline to complete last line
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(data) < MAX_SIZE:
        data += b"\n"

    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _compose(rng)
